title: A New Framework for Convex Clustering in Kernel Spaces: Finite Sample Bounds, Consistency and Performance Insights
summary: Convex clustering fails on linearly non-separable or non-convex data, and a prior kernelized formulation lacked implementation and theory. The paper reparameterizes kernel convex clustering via the representer theorem, uses Cholesky decomposition K=Z^T Z to reduce it to ordinary convex clustering of an embedding Z, and solves the resulting problem with ADMM. Empirically KCC gives strong NMI on real benchmarks, including 0.778 on Lymphoma, while the paper proves finite-sample bounds and consistency under weight and fusion-penalty conditions.

match_target.why: The user hint explicitly names Lymphoma/KCC/0.778, and this is a central real-data result that is cheap to run because n=96 and the kernel matrix is only 96x96.

tolerance.why: Rule 3: no std is reported, NMI is a bounded [0,1] metric on a small 96-point dataset, and the paper prints NMI as a fraction, so the tolerance is 0.02 absolute.

requirements.stmt: Implement the kernel convex clustering objective with a fit term and an L1 fusion penalty over centroids.
requirements.quote: The second term is a penalisation term, to keep the number of distinct centroids in check.

requirements.stmt: Use the representer theorem for this problem: each centroid lies in the span of the mapped data, so u_i = φ^T α_i.
requirements.quote: Thus u∗ i = φ⊤α∗ i for some α∗ i ∈Rn.

requirements.stmt: Use ADMM with auxiliary variables v_ij=a_i-a_j and Lagrange multipliers η_ij.

requirements.stmt: Use a Gaussian kernel, with the GLI85 motivating example using σ=0.001.

for every pair i̸ = j, wij = e−∥xi−xj∥2/2σ2 2 I[xj is one of the 6 nearest neighbours of xi].

requirements.stmt: Apply agglomerative clustering to the learned centroids and build a dendrogram.
requirements.quote: This is carried out, first by applying agglomerative clustering on the centroids, followed by constructing a dendrogram.

requirements.stmt: Select the number of clusters by SSE_k elbow analysis over dendrogram cuts.
requirements.quote: After computing SSEk for every k, we construct the elbow plot of SSEk vs. k.

requirements.stmt: For continuous-covariate benchmarks, center and scale each feature before KCC.
requirements.quote: For datasets with continuous covariates, we scale the data by centering each of the datasets and dividing by the corresponding variance.

requirements.stmt: Do not standardize Lymphoma because its features are discrete.

requirements.stmt: For MNIST, sample 50 images from each of 10 classes, giving 500 points total.

requirements.stmt: Evaluate cluster quality with Normalized Mutual Information.
requirements.quote: We use Normalized Mutual Information (NMI) (Vinh et al., 2010) to evaluate the quality of clustering.
